text:
Mira Chen: heads-up — I'm seeing a steady memory creep on streaming_toolloop-2 in prod since 03:00 UTC. Sessions with very long contexts (30k-60k tokens) drive the agent heap up ~1.1GB/day. KV cache total rises, but pprof shows a lot of 'slab' residency rather than obvious heap objects. :eyes:
Alex Park: any recent kernel-selection or batching changes rolled to that fleet?
Mira Chen: not that I know of, only a minor batching heuristic tweak last week (reduce max_batch_size from 64->48) which shouldn't cause this pattern.
Samir Patel: can you dump slab stats? slab-level fragmentation / pinned counts could point to sticky allocations.
Mira Chen: ran slab-inspector on gw-02, pasted below.
Samir Patel: nice, share it here.
Mira Chen: ```
kv_slab_summary: total=1.82GB pinned=912MB free_frag=436MB
epoch: 2025-10-03T03:45Z
hot_buckets: prefix_cache(38%), token_kv(27%), session_meta(8%)
slot_heatmap: tail-heavy with many entries in the 512-2048B bins
notes: high pinned count in prefix_cache across long sessions
```
Alex Park: that pinned=912MB looks suspicious. Do we have allocation-site info?
Mira Chen: I grabbed a small pprof snapshot from the runtime:
```
(pprof) top5
  34.2%  kv_put
  21.8%  prefix_insert
  12.5%  token_kv_write
  8.9%   session_alloc
  6.0%   buffer_append
```
Lee Zhao: hmm prefix_insert and kv_put dominating. Those are hot paths for streaming writes (tool loops append). Could be a reuse/regeneration bug where we pin many small pages and they never get reclaimed because of slab-anchoring when prefix TTLs are long.
Samir Patel: I pushed a quick binary to staging that enables aggressive slab coalescing and reduces prefix_ttl from 30m->5m. Would love a smoke run.
alloc-bot: deploy:staging/kv-optimize  - started by @samir - commit 1a2b3c - hosts: stg-*
Mira Chen: smoke run looks promising: memory delta stable over 30m vs baseline drift earlier. Need to be careful about correctness (we don't want to evict useful prefixes prematurely).
Alex Park: can we reproduce locally with a deterministic toolloop? Maybe run the long-context harness with a mixture of append+replace operations that mimic tool chains.
Mira Chen: repro steps I used:
  1) start local runtime with --kv-ttl=30m --kv-coalesce=off
  2) run reproducer: scripts/repro_toolloop_long.sh --sessions 200 --avg_tokens 45k
  3) observe slab summary every 5m via /admin/slab_stats
Samir Patel: attaching a tiny heap diff from staging (trimmed):
```
+908MB kv_slab.pinned (+312MB prefix_cache)
+120MB token_kv residual
-20MB temp buffers
```
Lee Zhao: hypothesis: after kernel change around kernel-selection v3.2 we altered the eviction path ordering when backpressure is present; eviction used to scan small pages first, now it prefers coalesced pages which leaves many small bins pinned. That interaction with streaming append patterns can cause fragmentation growth over long sessions.
Alex Park: good angle. Can we try reverting the eviction scan order in a feature branch and run the harness?
Samir Patel: creating branch "evict-scan-reverse-v2" and will run nightly harness. Also adding a metric export for slab_bin_counts per 1m so we can alert when small-bin fraction > 30%.
Mira Chen: created a support ticket PROD-9537 and added logs + pprof links (private). Putting a short mitigation list in the ticket:
  - temporarily lower kv-ttl for streaming customers
  - enable slab coalescing in prod on canary hosts
  - revert eviction-scan ordering if staging repros confirm
Alex Park: thanks. If repro passes, let's prepare a small rollout with canary 5% and tracing flags enabled. @Lee can you own the rollback plan?
Lee Zhao: will do. Plan: if small-bin fraction exceeds threshold or p50 memory jumps >200MB in canary -> automatic rollback.
Mira Chen: thanks team. I'll keep posting slab snapshots. Next update in ~2h after nightly harness run. :thumbsup:
